title: Ready a free-rolling wheelchair for a transfer: both wheel locks on, both footrests swung aside
instruction: Get the wheelchair ready for a transfer: lock both wheels and swing both footrests out of the way, without letting the chair roll.
context: Nursing assistants transport patients in wheelchairs and lift them on and off beds and tables (O*NET 31-1131.00 task statements, https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/31-1131.00); the chair is locked and its footrests cleared before such a transfer. This empty-chair task uses a full-size Drive Silver Sport 2 SSP218FA-SF with compatible STDS801GT extensions to engage both wheel locks and clear both swing-away footrests. Unlike accepted TK-T53PKY / PR #2280, which unfolds a chair with its footrests removed, it requires operating the rolling chair's existing brake and footrest mechanisms. No patient transfer is performed.
setup: One folding manual wheelchair, a Drive Medical Silver Sport 2 (model SSP218FA-SF, serial not starting 3J): steel frame, 18 x 16 in seat 19.5 in above the floor, fixed full-length arms, 24 in rear wheels with solid urethane tyres, 8 in swivel casters, 18.4 kg in all as modelled (the maker quotes 18.6 kg, 41 lb). It stands open and free on the floor facing the two arms, centred between them, its footplate front edges 7 cm in front of the arms' base line. Both push-to-lock wheel locks are off; each carries Drive's 8 in wheel-lock extension handle (STDS801GT; about 19 x 28 mm section, an estimate) slid over the lock handle in place of its rubber tip. Both swing-away footrests are latched pointing forward; each releases when the lever on the front of its hanger is pushed 3 mm into its 6 mm stroke (engineering estimates) and swings out sideways to a 90 degree stop. Ten 10 mm paper tape dots mark the stillness points named in the scoring (not drawn in the simulation, which tracks the same points). Nothing else is on the floor. The layout matches the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if the chair tips more than 10 degrees, if its reference point (the midpoint of the two front uprights at floor level) ends more than 5 cm, or its heading more than 5 degrees, from where it started, if any gripper jaw or pad point comes within 8 cm of the chair during the final 1 s, or if any of 10 tape marks moves 5 mm or more during the final 1 s (against a ruler in the video): one on each front upright at seat height, each push-handle end, each rear tyre's side wall, each lock extension's tip and each footplate's front edge. Otherwise 0.25 for each of these, as it is at the end: the left wheel lock engaged (its handle past centre), the right wheel lock engaged, the left footrest at least 80 degrees aside, the right footrest at least 80 degrees aside. Either order. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
fidelity: The chair is a rigid frame with hinged locks, hinged footrests with a sliding release lever, and free wheels; the lock's over-centre spring, the footrest latch and the locked-wheel hold are modelled drives. The extension's section and the footrest hinge friction (coefficient 0.040, about 0.043 N m breakaway) are estimates, not measured. Tyres are rigid, so a lock shoe does not dent its tyre. Seat fabric and cushions are omitted.
reset_notes: Pull both wheel locks back off, swing both footrests forward until they latch, and put the chair back on its floor marks.
